title: Directional Spline Minimums & Compact Billing Probe for Hosted API
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Overview: This ticket captures an experimental probe to evaluate a compacted billing model that applies asymmetric per-token minimums and a directional (input vs output) spline to smooth enterprise invoice volatility for heavy streaming workloads. The goal is to find a pragmatic trade-off between predictable revenue, reduced customer surprise on monthly bills, and maintaining low friction for PLG sign-ups.

Hypothesis: Introducing a compact billing path that compresses small-volume streaming spikes into a directional spline (higher floor on output tokens, lower floor on input tokens for conversational streams) will: (1) reduce support billing disputes by >= 30% for pilot accounts, (2) preserve or improve ARR from affected customers by +/- 5% within first 90 days, and (3) not materially reduce request volume or degrade latency SLOs.

Experimental Design:
- Cohorts: 1) Control (current per-token IO + streaming minimums), 2) Compact-Billing (directional spline floors applied), 3) Compact-Billing + Grace (same as 2 with 14-day grace crediting for first billing cycle).
- Sample: 200 mid-to-large hosted API customers filtered by average daily streaming output tokens >= 50k and at least 30 days tenure. Randomized at account level, blocked by enterprise/SQ status to avoid exposing high-risk contracts.
- Duration: 60 days active test + 30 days observation.
- Metrics: billing dispute rate (primary), net revenue retention for cohort, churn/usage delta, avg latency, support tickets volume, NPS delta for pilot customers.
- Statistical plan: Use difference-in-differences for revenue and two-proportion z-test for dispute rates; power calc targets detect 30% relative dispute reduction with alpha=0.05, power=0.8.

Telemetry & Instrumentation:
- New billing debug tags: compact_bill_variant, spline_parameters, grace_credit_flag.
- Dashboard: Billing Experiment Dashboard (grafana link in links) will show per-account daily invoiced tokens, raw tokens by direction, effective floor applied, and dispute events.
- Feature flag: rollout behind feature flag hosted.compact_billing.v1 with whitelist for pilot accounts.

Operational considerations:
- Invoicing: Finance will need a compacted ledger view that reconciles directional floors. Early prototype uses a separate invoice line item labeled 'Compact billing adjustment' to keep accounting auditable.
- Support: Provide support playbook and templated responses; train AE/CS on how compact floors will appear on invoices.
- Legal: Ensure pilot customers' EUL/contract amendments are minimal — boxed as addendum template in links.

Enterprise / Security Questionnaire (SQ) impacts:
- For pilot customers under active SQs we will not alter contract terms without explicit sales/legal approval. For new pilots, surface a short SQ addendum clarifying rounding, floor logic, and auditability; KMS/HSM not affected.
- Security review required because billing variant exposes additional per-account metadata and needs to confirm PII-free telemetry retention and RBAC for billing debug tags.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Pros: less frequent small disputes, smoother revenue recognition for irregular streaming workloads, clearer line items for customers who care about output-heavy costs.
- Cons: Risk of perceived higher unit cost for output tokens, potential churn from price-sensitive PLG users, accounting complexity. We prioritize reducing dispute noise for enterprise AR growth at small possible PLG friction.

Dependencies: ["PM-27103","PM-421987","PM-300527"]

Acceptance criteria:
- Technical: Feature flag implementation and instrumentation deployed to staging; Grafana dashboard populated with streaming token decomposition and applied floor per-account.
- Business: Achieve >= 30% reduction in dispute rates in Compact-Billing cohort vs Control, or surface clear qualitative reasons in post-mortem if not achieved.
- Compliance: Security review signed off and legal addendum template approved for pilots.

decisions: Use directional spline with stronger floor on output tokens and shallower floor on input tokens to favor conversational throughput use-cases.
Pilot will only include accounts with non-sensitive SQ status unless explicit Sales/Legal approval is provided.
Introduce grace cohort to test goodwill crediting impact on disputes and churn.

Post-mortem and go/no-go decision with Sales/Legal after observation window
